summary.headline: The largest logged gain: +4.3 percentage points at 48 hours.
summary.description: Better weather inputs lifted the earlier-feature model from 84.9% to 89.2% in the documented matched twelve-month experiment. The current corrected model scores 88.9%. The latest three experiments did not improve warnings enough to replace it. Read the timeline as development history: the test groups and evaluation rules changed along the way.

experiments.title: Check the official wind rules
experiments.outcome: On observed airport weather, the rules agree with recorded directions in 89.2% of hours. Rules are a comparison method, not the recorded truth.

experiments.title: First direction model
experiments.outcome: 93.8 / 91.5 / 90.8 / 89.8% at 1 / 6 / 24 / 48 h. Short-range forecasts lost to keeping the current direction. These early scores did not yet enforce the later six-hour weather publication delay.

experiments.title: Use the current direction
experiments.outcome: A blend with the current direction lifted 1 h accuracy from 93.8% to 96.9%. Historical source artifacts also show 6 h falling from 91.5% to 90.9%; the old log's 'others unchanged' wording is incorrect.

experiments.title: Allow for weather publication delay
experiments.outcome: A six-hour delay and older forecasts for long leads prevent overly fresh forecast inputs. Results became 97.0 / 91.5 / 90.3 / 84.1%. The lower 48 h score reflects a stricter test; do not present it as a model-quality decline.

experiments.title: Check training and command-line forecasts agree
experiments.outcome: On three October dates (144 lead rows), both paths produced identical features and probabilities.

experiments.title: Reconstruct October midnight forecasts
experiments.outcome: 84.2 / 79.0 / 75.7% in the 1–6 / 7–24 / 25–48 h lead groups. Keeping the current direction won at short range (95.3%). These are grouped leads from October, not the point-lead annual scores.

experiments.title: Extend observations back to 2018
experiments.outcome: Rebuilt 76,588 labelled hours. The direction archive spans eight years; the joined forecast model trains on inputs available from 2024. More archive history is not eight years of forecast training.

experiments.title: Treat runway 18 non-use as closure
experiments.outcome: Rejected: only one of 2,251 non-use hours met the north-tailwind threshold. Operational non-use is not a weather closure label.

experiments.title: Adapt the blend to operating conditions
experiments.outcome: v4 varies the blend by night, calm or active conditions and uses local-clock issue times. Its published six-month score is 94.6 / 90.7 / 89.6 / 84.9%. The later E12 comparison reran the earlier feature set on twelve months.

experiments.title: Investigate a rule-contradicting recorded run
experiments.outcome: A 103-hour October run contradicted the weather-rule expectation. v4/v5 excluded it from fitting and reported sensitivity scores; v6 retains all recorded directions for its primary fit. The discrepancy does not prove a faulty feed.

experiments.title: Give the model separate weather forecasts
experiments.outcome: ECMWF, GFS and ICON forecasts expose agreement, spread and corrected tailwinds. In the logged matched twelve-month comparison, 48 h accuracy rose 84.9% → 88.6%; Brier fell .108 → .084 (lower is better).

experiments.title: Correct weather-model wind speeds
experiments.outcome: Wind correction factors were fitted on 2024 data. Runway-18 weather closures remained rare and difficult to predict. The old partial-window counts are superseded by v6's complete-window evaluation.

experiments.title: Combine the successful features in v5
experiments.outcome: Matched twelve-month log: accuracy rose 95.5→96.0%, 92.0→92.8%, 90.3→91.7%, 84.9→89.2% at 1 / 6 / 24 / 48 h. Earlier-feature values are rounded log evidence; their row-level before artifact is not in the current bundle.

experiments.title: Add regional pressure patterns
experiments.outcome: Pressure differences around Frankfurt added roughly 0.1–0.6 percentage points by lead beyond the weather-model features. They are included in v5 and v6.

experiments.title: Try more complex tree models
experiments.outcome: Deeper trees, tailwind constraints, separate lead models and additional state features stayed within ±0.6 percentage points, with equal or worse Brier scores. No overall gain justified adoption.

experiments.title: Try high-resolution ensemble spread
experiments.outcome: The available ICON-D2 ensemble archive starts 29 July 2026. It cannot support the same twelve-month test used here; a shorter experiment remains possible.

experiments.title: Strengthen the rule baseline
experiments.outcome: Applying rules to corrected ensemble wind scored 95.6 / 88.8 / 89.2 / 85.8% at 1 / 6 / 24 / 48 h. This is a stronger comparator than the base-wind rules, not a new trained model.

experiments.title: Double the training issue frequency
experiments.outcome: Training every three hours instead of six brought no consistent gain on the same evaluation issues. The one-hour score worsened to 95.0%; the six-hour stride remained.

experiments.title: Add older observation-only training rows
experiments.outcome: About 52,000 rows from 2018–2023 lacked forecast features. Scores became 95.1 / 92.7 / 91.9 / 89.3%; the one-hour score worsened and later differences were small.

experiments.title: Use wind-speed-dependent corrections
experiments.outcome: Not pursued: the apparent stronger-wind bias depended on how observations were grouped. Fitting the correction on 2025–2026 would contaminate test months; fixed 2024 factors remain.

experiments.title: Add the latest forecast error
experiments.outcome: Features for observed-versus-forecast tailwind and one-hour wind trend were coded, but the walk-forward run did not finish before the freeze. No measured gain; not served.

experiments.title: Add air-pressure observations and trend
experiments.outcome: METAR pressure and its three-hour tendency were prepared, but not evaluated before the freeze. No measured gain; not served.

experiments.title: Label calm variable-wind hours for runway 18
experiments.outcome: A rule clarification would add about 2,067 easy usable hours. It requires retraining and was not applied to the served model. Higher overall accuracy from these labels would not establish better closure detection.

experiments.title: Correct state handling and event evaluation in v6
experiments.outcome: Current scores: 95.7 / 92.7 / 91.8 / 88.9%. Carries observed tailwind duration into rules, tightens input availability, restores all recorded OD labels, and evaluates unique change events and complete runway-18 windows. No broad accuracy gain over v5.

experiments.title: Independent October learner comparison
experiments.outcome: The earlier v4 comparison recomputed 72/72 metric rows. Alternative learners did not establish a replacement. This was an October-only comparison against that historical model, not against current v6.

experiments.title: Fresh independent raw-ICON comparison
experiments.outcome: Two completed external CPU runs tested six- and twelve-hour availability assumptions on a restricted 2025+ training set and October target hours. Added ICON features improved some 48 h scores but not all horizons; paired seven-day Brier intervals included zero. No model promoted. These cohorts differ from current v6.

experiments.title: Predict a different direction directly
experiments.outcome: July–October: 42 of 67 events matched versus 44 for v6; false-alarm groups rose from 50 to 59. Small gains at one lead did not justify the worse overall event result.

experiments.title: Mix learned probabilities with physical rules
experiments.outcome: July–October, separately restricted complete windows: both methods matched 41 of 65 events; false-alarm groups rose from 49 to 53. The 48 h score also worsened.

experiments.title: Predict the first change within a time window
experiments.outcome: July–October: both methods matched 44 of 67 events, but false-alarm groups rose from 50 to 138. The new target learned a useful probability signal at 6–48 h, yet its fixed warning threshold did not improve warnings.

challengers.label: Different direction
challengers.note: July–October 2026; 467 valid forecast windows. Same event population as first-change test.

challengers.label: Model + physical rules
challengers.note: July–October 2026; 443 valid windows after a different month-boundary restriction. Compare within this row, not with the other rows.

challengers.label: First change within a window
challengers.note: July–October 2026; 467 valid windows; fixed 0.5 warning threshold. Probability of any change is a different target from hourly direction.

limits: All dates and times on this page are Berlin time. Version timestamps are Git records of saved results, not measured training completion times. They cannot establish how long an idea took.
Each monthly model was trained on earlier data. These test months also informed development; no untouched prospective test or operational acceptance is claimed.
Early scores used different availability rules, issue schedules or numbers of test months. Do not subtract arbitrary timeline rows or plot them as one accuracy-growth curve.

The matched E12 improvement uses rounded figures in the experiment log. Its v5 result has a saved evaluation artifact; the earlier-feature per-row predictions are not included in the current source bundle.

v5 to v6 has the same lead-specific evaluation counts but changes fitting and scoring: accuracy moved −0.28 / −0.07 / +0.14 / −0.30 percentage points at 1 / 6 / 24 / 48 h. More reliable state and event accounting is not a broad accuracy jump.
Current v6 matches 115 of 193 unique recorded direction changes within ±3 h, with 138 false-alarm groups. Earlier scores on overlapping change windows measured a different thing.

Runway 18 remains weak: 0 warnings in 12 positive 24 h windows among 307 complete windows; 1,125 windows excluded. Labels are inferred from weather, not actual runway closures. The positive windows overlap.
DFLD is a public proxy for operations. A weather-rule contradiction does not prove the recorded direction is wrong. Windy connection-test values do not enter these models.
The independent October comparisons use restricted data and historical reference models. Their scores cannot be used as an accuracy gain against current twelve-month v6.

independent_review.description: Hugo’s merged PR #3 adds reviewer reports, executed notebook evidence and independent recalculation of the recorded results. These checks support the evidence trail; they are not another accuracy increase.

checks.label: Completed external training runs
checks.note: Colab CPU runs completed with six-hour and twelve-hour weather-availability assumptions. Both exited successfully; roughly 287 seconds each.

checks.label: Tests on the frozen source
checks.note: The recorded source snapshot passed its existing test suite before training. This is a historical test result, separate from current-main test totals.

checks.label: Original result rows recalculated
checks.note: Forty headline metric rows per availability assumption were recomputed from prediction traces. The expanded audit CSV contains 88 rows; these are metric rows, not additional flights or models.

checks.label: Version-ledger rows checked
checks.note: An independent review matched the ledger to notebook results, the audited CSV or pinned historical v5/v6 artifacts. Historical v5/v6 rows were not independently retrained.

independent_review.outcome: Decision: keep the served v6 model. Added ICON weather features improved some long-range results, but did not show a consistent advantage across forecast leads. Model selection by weather conditions also gave mixed results. Neither candidate was promoted.
limits: The paired October experiment uses restricted 2025+ training data: 122,280 training rows and 5,068 scored direction rows. It is not the twelve-month evaluation of current v6.

Both runs use the same original 45 features and matched rows within each comparison; the ICON candidate adds seven weather features. Six- and twelve-hour delays are availability assumptions, not verified historical publication times.
Seven-day paired uncertainty intervals include zero for all nonzero primary Brier differences. The apparent small gains do not establish a general improvement.
The October runway-18 comparison has no closure-positive complete windows. Its 100% hourly accuracy is not proof of detecting closures.
Some archived tests demonstrate a problematic case, and suite totals overlap. Their passing counts must not be added together or described as proof that every reported weakness was fixed.
No causal reduction in Frankfurt delays or financial savings was measured. October informed development; a fresh forward test is still needed.
